闇.meaning: The <part>gate</part> at the edge of town has a <part>chime</part> hanging from its bar. Each time the wind rings it, one lamp in town blinks out, then one star, then the moon. By the hundredth ding nobody can see their own hands: it has begun to <kanji>get dark</kanji>.
闇.on: Your <sound>un</sound>cle stumbles home holding up one birthday candle.
闇.kun: From the pitch black a voice calls, '<sound>Ya</sound>hoo, it's <sound>me</sound>!', and he drops the candle.

煩.meaning: Someone sets a scented candle on the edge of the bath, right next to a <part>rubber duck</part>. The little <part>fire</part> flickers closer every time the water ripples. The duck can't relax: is my tail going soft? Am I melting? Pure <kanji>anxiety</kanji>.
煩.on: To calm its nerves it sips warm <sound>hon</sound>ey tea.
煩.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' squeaks the duck as a yu<sound>zu</sound> rolls into the bath and splashes its <sound>ra</sound>men.

据.meaning: A family wants to <part>reside</part> on a houseboat, but it drifts off every night. So Grandma drops a huge <part>anchor</part>, parks the piano on top of it and plants her rocking chair in the middle of the deck. Nothing moves now: everything is <kanji>set</kanji>.
据.on: Her neighbour opens a tiny floating <sound>kio</sound>sk that sells tea.
据.kun: Grandma sets a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi on the piano lid.

漠.meaning: A painter finishes a perfect <part>sunset</part> on a sea cliff, then rain spatters <part>water drops</part> all over the canvas. Sun, grass and sea run into one soft orange smudge. Buyers squint and guess: a fox? a teapot? It's all very <kanji>vague</kanji>.
漠.on: A cowboy buys it anyway, paying with his shiny belt <sound>buc</sound>kle.

滝.meaning: A <part>dragon</part> squeezes into a mountain lake for a bath. The water spills over the cliff edge, and the <part>water drops</part> become a roaring curtain falling into the valley. Every time it scrubs its back, the <kanji>waterfall</kanji> doubles.
滝.on: It drops in a <sound>ro</sound>se bath bomb, and the whole cliff turns pink.
滝.kun: Down below, hikers eat a <sound>ta</sound>co and a <sound>ki</sound>wi in the pink spray.

尉.meaning: Under the prison <part>flag</part>, a bored guard sets up mini golf in the yard: an old stone <part>altar</part> as a ramp, a mop for a <part>golf club</part>. Prisoners fetch his stray golf balls, and whoever sinks a putt gets extra pudding. He's the jolliest <kanji>jailer</kanji> around.
尉.on: One prisoner keeps a pet <sound>ee</sound>l hidden in the hole.

塞.meaning: A badger's den has a hole in its <part>roof</part>. She lays <part>one</part> plank across it, then <part>eight</part> pebbles, then a big mound of <part>soil</part> on top, patting it flat with her paws. The rain can't get in now: she's managed to <kanji>close</kanji> it.
塞.on: The last little gap she stuffs with an old striped <sound>sock</sound>.
塞.kun: Then she drags her <sound>fu</sound>ton under the patch and lies there munching a <sound>sa</sound>rdine.
